context:
Land per-platform in separate PRs under this one TODO's work units; each
platform migration ships with a before/after DDL snapshot test proving the
rendered statements are intentional (identical, or a documented improvement).
description:
From the 2026-07-12 tuning review, findings C5 (policy side), R2/R3 (structural
side), architecture assessment (evidence pinned to commit acfb8992). GATED on
ADR-3 (tuning-adr-baseline-definition-and-renderer-20260712).

Implements the decided direction:
- ONE capability registry keyed by canonical platform type; the six current
  sources (interface.py compat map, generator registry,
  platform_capabilities.py, adapter mixins, `benchbox tuning platforms`
  tables, coverage matrix) become derivations or lookups of it;
- ONE rendering path shared by dry-run preview and execution (per ADR-3,
  expected: adapters consume core/tuning/generators/*); delete dead renderers
  (clickhouse generate_tuning_clause has zero callers) and log-only apply
  paths become real or explicitly declared no-capability;
- BASELINE POLICY per ADR-3: relocate/record the ClickHouse OLAP session pack
  (clickhouse/tuning.py:74-100), label engine-mandatory layout (StarRocks
  DISTRIBUTED BY injection) in bundle metadata, and align the databricks-liquid
  warn-vs-fail behavior with the recorded policy axis;
- Databricks-specific layout validation moves out of interface.py
  (_validate_databricks_effective_layout) into the platform layer.

anti_patterns.dont: No big-bang rewrite across all platforms in one PR
delete a mixin path before its generator replacement has a snapshot test

preserves.behavior: Existing bundle schema compatibility during migration (renderer change must not silently change published metadata semantics without a schema note)
Physical rendering identity boundaries (zorder vs liquid auto/manual vs duckdb tuned) per the databricks-liquid TODO must_preserve

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/tuning/ddl_generator.py get_ddl_generator: registry seed — extend into the capability registry
benchbox/platforms/base/format_capabilities.py: existing per-platform capability declaration pattern — reuse shape
docs/development/adapter-refactor-map.md: prior slice-by-slice platform refactor process — reuse

work_units.notes:
Added benchbox/core/tuning/capability_registry.py: PLATFORM_TUNING_CAPABILITIES
maps canonical platform type -> {TuningType: TuningCapability(rendered_via,
mechanism_id, notes)}, derived from get_ddl_generator's registry,
interface.py's historical compatibility map, and direct adapter/mixin
inspection. Covers the 9 platforms interface.py already knew (duckdb,
snowflake, bigquery, redshift, clickhouse, databricks, sqlite, postgresql,
mysql) plus starrocks and doris (explicitly named by this TODO / w2).

interface.py's _PLATFORM_COMPATIBILITY_MAP and _KNOWN_COMPATIBILITY_PLATFORMS
are now computed from capability_registry.interface_compatibility_map()
instead of hand-duplicated (deferred import inside a module-level helper
to avoid the interface<->registry import cycle; registry imports TuningType
from interface, which is already defined by the time the helper runs).
platform_capabilities.py's map_candidate_to_platform dispatch now checks
membership in capability_registry.WORKLOAD_PROFILE_MAPPED_PLATFORMS
instead of an implicit if/elif fallthrough.

NO is_compatible_with_platform behavior changes shipped. One candidate
was investigated and rejected: Databricks TuningType.DISTRIBUTION looked
like a dead compatibility entry (no adapter renders a literal
DISTRIBUTED-BY clause for it), but shipped tuned examples
(examples/tunings/databricks/tpch_tuned.yaml, tpcds_tuned.yaml, etc.) set
`distribution:` columns that the Z-ORDER workload-profile mapping folds
into ZORDER locality upstream of the adapter -- removing the entry would
have newly hard-errored those shipped configs. Documented in the
registry's module docstring instead of changed.

test_capability_source_drift.py did not exist yet (the TODO's prompt
assumed prior scaffolding that wasn't present in this repo state), so it
was authored fresh with strict/empty EXPECTED_INTERFACE_VS_REGISTRY_DRIFT
(interface.py's map is now literally `==` the registry's derivation, not
just "consistent"), plus two non-empty, reasoned allowlists documenting
real remaining gaps this TODO did not close: ~12 DDL-generator-registered
platform aliases (trino, presto, athena, firebolt, azure_synapse/synapse,
timescaledb, questdb, pg-duckdb/pg_duckdb, pg-mooncake/pg_mooncake) with
no capability_registry entry yet, since none of them are in this TODO's
w2 migration order.
work_units.summary: Introduce the capability registry; derive interface compat checks and platform_capabilities from it; consistency test flips from allowlist-drift to strict

work_units.notes:
Scope note vs. the original summary: migration order was duckdb ->
clickhouse -> starrocks per this implementation's explicit brief; the
unmerged PR #1176 conflict-avoidance note additionally kept this round
out of benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py and result_capture.py.

DuckDB (done): _build_duckdb_ctas_sort_sql (shared by DuckDB and
MotherDuck adapters, the real post-load CTAS-sort execution path via
SortedIngestionMixin.apply_ctas_sort) now delegates to
core.tuning.generators.duckdb.DuckDBDDLGenerator via a TableTuning,
instead of hand-building the ORDER BY string. Output text is unchanged
(proven by tests/unit/core/tuning/test_renderer_snapshot_duckdb.py:
preview's tuning_clauses.sort_by text appears verbatim in the executed
CTAS statement). Existing unit tests using Mock column objects were
updated to real TuningColumn instances, since the generator's
TableTuning input validates column identifiers via isinstance.

ClickHouse (done): before this round, ClickHouse's real create_schema
execution path never consumed table_tunings (partitioning/sorting/
clustering columns) at all -- _optimize_table_definition only ran the
engine-mandatory PK-derived-or-ORDER-BY-tuple() fallback in every
tuning mode, while dry-run preview rendered (unused) PARTITION BY/ORDER
BY text via the generator. Tuned table_tunings now actually render
PARTITION BY/ORDER BY at CREATE TABLE time via the same
ClickHouseDDLGenerator dry-run preview uses
(ClickHouseWorkloadMixin._resolve_tuned_ddl_clauses), gated on
self.tuning_enabled so baseline/notuning keeps only the
PK-derived-or-tuple() fallback (that fallback is the untuned/
engine-mandatory path per ADR-3 and is unchanged). Deleted
ClickHouseTuningMixin.generate_tuning_clause (reconfirmed zero
production callers via `rg -n "\.generate_tuning_clause\("`) and its
four dead-code unit tests. Proof:
tests/unit/core/tuning/test_renderer_snapshot_clickhouse.py. Verified
both dry-run and a live chdb run (`benchbox run --platform
clickhouse-local --benchmark tpch --scale 0.01 --tuning tuned`)
complete successfully with the new path active; no shipped ClickHouse
tuning example templates exist yet in examples/tunings/, so the CLI
dry-run ddl_preview itself stayed empty in that smoke check -- the
generator-call-path proof is the direct unit-constructed-TableTuning
snapshot tests, not the CLI smoke run.

StarRocks (explicitly scoped out of migration, registry entry only):
no benchbox.core.tuning.ddl_generator entry exists for "starrocks" and
this TODO explicitly forbids writing one this round. Confirmed
StarRocksTuningMixin.apply_table_tunings only logs configured
partitioning/sorting/distribution columns -- never renders them --
and workload.py's schema rewrite unconditionally appends `DISTRIBUTED
BY HASH(<first_column>) BUCKETS 8` when no distribution clause is
already present, in every tuning mode; that unconditional injection is
kept exactly as-is (engine-mandatory baseline, not a tuned
DISTRIBUTED-BY-key choice -- StarRocks requires a distribution clause
for a working table). capability_registry's "starrocks" entry records
all three tuning types as rendered_via="none" with reasons
distinguishing the log-only gap (partitioning/sorting) from the
engine-mandatory-baseline gap (distribution). No code changes to
benchbox/platforms/starrocks/*.

Databricks (explicitly scoped out per this implementation's brief --
"SKIP migration (liquid work is owned by the blocked databricks
TODO); registry entry only"): capability_registry records Databricks'
current real behavior (PARTITIONING -> Delta PARTITIONED BY via the
cloud_spark DDL mixin; CLUSTERING/Z_ORDERING/LIQUID_CLUSTERING ->
post-load OPTIMIZE ZORDER BY / ALTER TABLE CLUSTER BY;
AUTO_OPTIMIZE/AUTO_COMPACT -> Delta TBLPROPERTIES; DISTRIBUTION,
BLOOM_FILTERS, MATERIALIZED_VIEWS -> none/unimplemented) without
touching benchbox/platforms/databricks/adapter.py's tuning-rendering
code. This is the "third rendering universe" ADR-3 calls out
(SparkDDLGeneratorMixin) and needs its own migration/equivalence pass,
which the blocked databricks-liquid-clustering-tuning-review-20260526
TODO owns.
work_units.summary: Renderer unification per ADR-3, one platform at a time starting duckdb -> clickhouse -> starrocks; dry-run preview calls the same renderer as execution

work_units.notes:
ClickHouseTuningMixin.configure_for_benchmark's OLAP session pack
(join_algorithm=grace_hash, grace_hash_join_initial_buckets,
optimize_aggregation_in_order, group_by_two_level_threshold, 50%-memory
spill thresholds for external group-by/sort, 50%-memory max_bytes_in_join)
now fires when `self.tuning_enabled` is True instead of False -- the
exact inversion ADR-3 flagged. The basic settings (max_memory_usage,
max_execution_time, max_threads, use_uncompressed_cache,
enable_optimize_predicate_expression, allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries)
and cache-control settings (use_query_cache family, gated on
disable_result_cache) are unchanged: harness-operational, they already
applied in every mode. Pinned in
tests/unit/platforms/test_clickhouse_adapter.py:
test_configure_for_benchmark_tuning_disabled_is_baseline_only asserts
grace_hash/optimize_aggregation_in_order are ABSENT even for an "olap"
benchmark type when tuning is disabled;
test_configure_for_benchmark_tuning_enabled_applies_olap_pack asserts
they're present when tuning is enabled. Also updated the
join-memory-multiplier and embedded-mode tests, which previously set
tuning_enabled=False to reach the OLAP branch -- now set True.

StarRocks DISTRIBUTED BY engine-mandatory labeling and ClickHouse/
StarRocks session-SET-statement bundle-ledger recording were NOT
implemented here: per the governing ADR-3 "Consequences" section, the
recording half of baseline policy (bundle ledger entries in every
mode) is explicitly the separate, gated
tuning-applied-ledger-and-validation-status-20260712 TODO's job, not
this one's. This TODO's w1 capability_registry documents the
engine-mandatory-vs-tuned distinction in its "notes" fields (consumed
by both the drift test and `benchbox tuning platforms`), which is the
labeling contribution in scope here.

`benchbox tuning platforms`'s SQL table (cli/commands/tuning_group.py)
is now generated from capability_registry.PLATFORM_TUNING_CAPABILITIES
(_sql_platform_capability_rows helper) instead of a hand-written
platform/feature-description list -- columns are now "Compatible
Tuning Types" and "Rendering" (flags any rendered_via="none" gaps per
platform) rather than free-text prose. The DataFrame table is
unchanged (out of registry scope, per this implementation's brief).
work_units.summary: Baseline policy enforcement: session-pack relocation + engine-mandatory layout labeling + `benchbox tuning platforms` output generated from the registry

work_units.notes:
UnifiedTuningConfiguration._validate_databricks_effective_layout moved
verbatim (same conditions, same error message text) to
benchbox/platforms/databricks/tuning_validation.py::validate_effective_layout,
taking `config: UnifiedTuningConfiguration` as a parameter instead of
`self`. interface.py's validate_for_platform_detailed now reaches it
through a small dispatch hook (_PLATFORM_EFFECTIVE_LAYOUT_VALIDATORS,
a dict of canonical platform key -> "module:function" resolved via
importlib.import_module + getattr at validation time) instead of a
hardcoded `if platform_key == "databricks": self._validate_databricks...()`
branch whose implementation lived in this module. Behavior verified
identical against the existing Liquid Clustering validation tests
(test_platform_optimization_config.py,
test_platform_identity_keys.py) and a direct reproduction of the
distribution-conflict error message.
work_units.summary: Move Databricks layout validation to the platform layer; slim interface.py to pure data model
